data.narrative:
Augury is a Series F robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz that has raised $369M to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Locus Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the narrow peer set—only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage comparable with similar valuation characteristics—is insufficient to support a reliable peer-median approach; an all-sector median would lack specificity given the diversity within robotics and manufacturing.

The stage-progression method is applicable and yields the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($369M) as a proxy baseline and applying a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x implies a valuation of $480M. This methodology reflects the incremental value creation between financing rounds in late-stage venture contexts.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $408M to $552M, centered on a $480M median. This range reflects a ±15% band around the point estimate derived from stage-progression. Key uncertainties remain: the narrow availability of directly comparable firms at this stage and valuation tier limits the ability to validate the 1.3x multiplier against peer evidence, and the sector's heterogeneity (spanning hardware, software, and hybrid models) creates ambiguity around appropriate step-up rates for this specific company.
